Note: two half-full trays count as one full tray.
maximal speed deviation from nominal, e.g. with nominal speed 70% and range 15%, the controller will assume speed between 55% and 85%. Note: Parameter = 0% means speed controller is disabled.

Proportional gain. Warning! Too high value may make speed unstable. \n Fill level controller - try to keep number of available free products close to setpoint (e.g. half of chain is empty).\n Control gain proportional to current fill level error. Tip: set kP = 2.3/t90, where t90 is desired time to reduce fill level error by 90%
Integral gain. Warning! Too high value may make speed unstable. \n Fill level controller - try to keep number of available free products close to setpoint (e.g. half of chain is empty).\n

Enable wait with pick until any place position is ready. Benefit: almost never have to drop product in garbage. Drawback: slight performance decrease for irregular product flows

When machine is stopped by operator and robot still has products on tool, then the robot will wait for X seconds for placing the product. After this time runs out, product that could not be placed will be dropped on "garbage" position

For multipick or multiplace only. Multipick) do not allow picking with finger 3 before products are present on fingers 1 and 2 - pick order is from first to last, i.e. pick finger 1, then finger 2, etc. - for multi-finger picking, only the lowest finger is checked. ******************************************************************************************* Multiplace) do not allow placing with finger 2 while products still present on fingers 3 or 4 - place order is from last to first, i.e. place finger 4, then place finger 3, then place finger 2, then 1 - for multi-finger placing, only the highest finger is checked.

Additional setting for the "Shortest way orientation" feature. Number of symmetry angles for valid pick&place. 0 = product can be picked/placed at ANY angle (e.g. circle product, cookie) 1 = Default. Only one valid pick/place angle, modulo 360° (e.g. half-circle product, taco) 2 = Two valid pick/place angles, modulo 180° (e.g. rectangle product, bar) 3 = Three valid pick/place angles, modulo 120° (e.g. triangle product, samosa) 4 = Four valid pick/place angles, modulo 90° (e.g. square product, bisquit)
Number of parts per element in a pick position (e.g. number of products per box or pocket to pick/place)
Number of elements per pick position (e.g. number of pockets to pick from or number of boxes to load)
TRUE = prioritize elements with minimal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities

Limit picking/placing only until certain fill level (total nbr of layers in all parts). For examle Limit=4 when picking will allow robot only to pick from containers with more than 4 products. Limit=4 when placing will allow robot only to place into containers with less than 4 products

[mm] nominal spacing between the DR elements to manage. For example, distance between PCC pockets to pick from or distance between boxes to place into. Note: elements might be skipped, e.g. with PCC pocket width 40mm you may set this parameter to 80mm --> every second pocket will be picked
[mm] tolerance for considering element spacing OK. For example, distance between boxes should be 300mm with tolerance plus-minus 5mm
TRUE = prioritize elements with minimal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = prioritize elements with maximal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = in multipart element, parts must be finished in order (do not select part[3] before part[2]); FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = in multipart element, one layer must be finished in all parts before starting next layer; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
Specific 32-bit status DWORD used for product type: 0 = UNDEFINED; 1 = TYPE A; 2 = TYPE B; 4 = TYPE C; 8 = TYPE D; 15 = ANY TYPE (A or B or C or D)
TRUE = Prioritize parts to balance number of products per meter on the flow; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
(has no effect when density balance is disabled) TRUE = Balancing within product types; FALSE = default, balancing within all products of all types
window around a part where density is evaluated (e.g. for window 500mm we evaluate all parts -+250mm away from this part in flow direction)

selection of location priority
 0 = RANDOM. default: randomly choose from aligible pick/place targets
 1 = RIGHT_TO_LEFT. prioritize right side of the flow (Y-) 
 2 = LEFT_TO_RIGHT. prioritize left side of the flow (Y+) 
 3 = FIFO. prioritize end of the flow (X+) 
 4 = LIFO. prioritize start of the flow (X-) 
 5 = NEAR_LINE_X. prioritize in flow direction closest to XRef 
 6 = NEAR_LINE_Y. prioritize in cross direction closest to YRef 
 7 = NEAR_POINT_XY. prioritize closest to the point (XRef, YRef) 
 8 = SHORTEST_TIME. prioritize closest to robot's current position and orientation

Enable wait with pick until any place position is ready. Benefit: almost never have to drop product in garbage. Drawback: slight performance decrease for irregular product flows

When machine is stopped by operator and robot still has products on tool, then the robot will wait for X seconds for placing the product. After this time runs out, product that could not be placed will be dropped on "garbage" position

For multipick or multiplace only. Multipick) do not allow picking with finger 3 before products are present on fingers 1 and 2 - pick order is from first to last, i.e. pick finger 1, then finger 2, etc. - for multi-finger picking, only the lowest finger is checked. ******************************************************************************************* Multiplace) do not allow placing with finger 2 while products still present on fingers 3 or 4 - place order is from last to first, i.e. place finger 4, then place finger 3, then place finger 2, then 1 - for multi-finger placing, only the highest finger is checked.

Additional setting for the "Shortest way orientation" feature. Number of symmetry angles for valid pick&place. 0 = product can be picked/placed at ANY angle (e.g. circle product, cookie) 1 = Default. Only one valid pick/place angle, modulo 360° (e.g. half-circle product, taco) 2 = Two valid pick/place angles, modulo 180° (e.g. rectangle product, bar) 3 = Three valid pick/place angles, modulo 120° (e.g. triangle product, samosa) 4 = Four valid pick/place angles, modulo 90° (e.g. square product, bisquit)
Number of parts per element in a pick position (e.g. number of products per box or pocket to pick/place)
Number of elements per pick position (e.g. number of pockets to pick from or number of boxes to load)
TRUE = prioritize elements with minimal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities

Limit picking/placing only until certain fill level (total nbr of layers in all parts). For examle Limit=4 when picking will allow robot only to pick from containers with more than 4 products. Limit=4 when placing will allow robot only to place into containers with less than 4 products

[mm] nominal spacing between the DR elements to manage. For example, distance between PCC pockets to pick from or distance between boxes to place into. Note: elements might be skipped, e.g. with PCC pocket width 40mm you may set this parameter to 80mm --> every second pocket will be picked
[mm] tolerance for considering element spacing OK. For example, distance between boxes should be 300mm with tolerance plus-minus 5mm
TRUE = prioritize elements with minimal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = prioritize elements with maximal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = in multipart element, parts must be finished in order (do not select part[3] before part[2]); FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = in multipart element, one layer must be finished in all parts before starting next layer; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
Specific 32-bit status DWORD used for product type: 0 = UNDEFINED; 1 = TYPE A; 2 = TYPE B; 4 = TYPE C; 8 = TYPE D; 15 = ANY TYPE (A or B or C or D)
TRUE = Prioritize parts to balance number of products per meter on the flow; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
(has no effect when density balance is disabled) TRUE = Balancing within product types; FALSE = default, balancing within all products of all types
window around a part where density is evaluated (e.g. for window 500mm we evaluate all parts -+250mm away from this part in flow direction)

selection of location priority
 0 = RANDOM. default: randomly choose from aligible pick/place targets
 1 = RIGHT_TO_LEFT. prioritize right side of the flow (Y-) 
 2 = LEFT_TO_RIGHT. prioritize left side of the flow (Y+) 
 3 = FIFO. prioritize end of the flow (X+) 
 4 = LIFO. prioritize start of the flow (X-) 
 5 = NEAR_LINE_X. prioritize in flow direction closest to XRef 
 6 = NEAR_LINE_Y. prioritize in cross direction closest to YRef 
 7 = NEAR_POINT_XY. prioritize closest to the point (XRef, YRef) 
 8 = SHORTEST_TIME. prioritize closest to robot's current position and orientation
<CCS> reference value X for location priority
<CCS> reference value Y for location priority

Specific 32-bit status DWORD used for product type: 0 = UNDEFINED; 1 = TYPE A; 2 = TYPE B; 4 = TYPE C; 8 = TYPE D; 15 = ANY TYPE (A or B or C or D)

selection of location priority
 0 = RANDOM. default: randomly choose from aligible pick/place targets
 1 = RIGHT_TO_LEFT. prioritize right side of the flow (Y-) 
 2 = LEFT_TO_RIGHT. prioritize left side of the flow (Y+) 
 3 = FIFO. prioritize end of the flow (X+) 
 4 = LIFO. prioritize start of the flow (X-) 
 5 = NEAR_LINE_X. prioritize in flow direction closest to XRef 
 6 = NEAR_LINE_Y. prioritize in cross direction closest to YRef 
 7 = NEAR_POINT_XY. prioritize closest to the point (XRef, YRef) 
 8 = SHORTEST_TIME. prioritize closest to robot's current position and orientation
<CCS> reference value X for location priority
<CCS> reference value Y for location priority

[mm] nominal spacing between the DR elements to manage. For example, distance between PCC pockets to pick from or distance between boxes to place into. Note: elements might be skipped, e.g. with PCC pocket width 40mm you may set this parameter to 80mm --> every second pocket will be picked
[mm] tolerance for considering element spacing OK. For example, distance between boxes should be 300mm with tolerance plus-minus 5mm

With this parameter it's possible to enable the parking mode for all units of this SM, depending on the loaded format. On active parking mode, the units will move to the home positions (parking positions). The production procedure won't be executed.

Maximum time the product is held on the gripper. If the time is expired and garbage is enabled, the product will be placed on the garbage position. Value 0 also deactivates this function. Very small value is not allowed, since robot needs time to place product.

Enable wait with pick until any place position is ready. Benefit: almost never have to drop product in garbage. Drawback: slight performance decrease for irregular product flows

When machine is stopped by operator and robot still has products on tool, then the robot will wait for X seconds for placing the product. After this time runs out, product that could not be placed will be dropped on "garbage" position

For multipick or multiplace only. Multipick) do not allow picking with finger 3 before products are present on fingers 1 and 2 - pick order is from first to last, i.e. pick finger 1, then finger 2, etc. - for multi-finger picking, only the lowest finger is checked. ******************************************************************************************* Multiplace) do not allow placing with finger 2 while products still present on fingers 3 or 4 - place order is from last to first, i.e. place finger 4, then place finger 3, then place finger 2, then 1 - for multi-finger placing, only the highest finger is checked.

Additional setting for the "Shortest way orientation" feature. Number of symmetry angles for valid pick&place. 0 = product can be picked/placed at ANY angle (e.g. circle product, cookie) 1 = Default. Only one valid pick/place angle, modulo 360° (e.g. half-circle product, taco) 2 = Two valid pick/place angles, modulo 180° (e.g. rectangle product, bar) 3 = Three valid pick/place angles, modulo 120° (e.g. triangle product, samosa) 4 = Four valid pick/place angles, modulo 90° (e.g. square product, bisquit)
Number of parts per element in a pick position (e.g. number of products per box or pocket to pick/place)
Number of elements per pick position (e.g. number of pockets to pick from or number of boxes to load)
TRUE = prioritize elements with minimal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities

Limit picking/placing only until certain fill level (total nbr of layers in all parts). For examle Limit=4 when picking will allow robot only to pick from containers with more than 4 products. Limit=4 when placing will allow robot only to place into containers with less than 4 products

[mm] nominal spacing between the DR elements to manage. For example, distance between PCC pockets to pick from or distance between boxes to place into. Note: elements might be skipped, e.g. with PCC pocket width 40mm you may set this parameter to 80mm --> every second pocket will be picked
[mm] tolerance for considering element spacing OK. For example, distance between boxes should be 300mm with tolerance plus-minus 5mm
TRUE = prioritize elements with minimal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = prioritize elements with maximal total number of layers; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = in multipart element, parts must be finished in order (do not select part[3] before part[2]); FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
TRUE = in multipart element, one layer must be finished in all parts before starting next layer; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
Specific 32-bit status DWORD used for product type: 0 = UNDEFINED; 1 = TYPE A; 2 = TYPE B; 4 = TYPE C; 8 = TYPE D; 15 = ANY TYPE (A or B or C or D)
TRUE = Prioritize parts to balance number of products per meter on the flow; FALSE = default, parts will be selected based on other priorities
(has no effect when density balance is disabled) TRUE = Balancing within product types; FALSE = default, balancing within all products of all types
window around a part where density is evaluated (e.g. for window 500mm we evaluate all parts -+250mm away from this part in flow direction)

selection of location priority
 0 = RANDOM. default: randomly choose from aligible pick/place targets
 1 = RIGHT_TO_LEFT. prioritize right side of the flow (Y-) 
 2 = LEFT_TO_RIGHT. prioritize left side of the flow (Y+) 
 3 = FIFO. prioritize end of the flow (X+) 
 4 = LIFO. prioritize start of the flow (X-) 
 5 = NEAR_LINE_X. prioritize in flow direction closest to XRef 
 6 = NEAR_LINE_Y. prioritize in cross direction closest to YRef 
 7 = NEAR_POINT_XY. prioritize closest to the point (XRef, YRef) 
 8 = SHORTEST_TIME. prioritize closest to robot's current position and orientation
<CCS> reference value X for location priority
<CCS> reference value Y for location priority
